metadata.title: Anthropic signs $45 billion cloud computing deal with Nscale

content.text:
Anthropic has signed a roughly $45 billion cloud computing deal with Nscale, a U.K.-based AI infrastructure company. Two confidential sources told CNBC that under the terms of the deal, Anthropic will lease roughly 460 megawatts of computing power from an Nscale data center facility in West Virginia.
The deal spans six years and will draw on Nvidia's Vera Rubin chips, according to TechCrunch. The Vera Rubin architecture integrates six distinct chips and represents the leading edge of what is technically achievable in chip engineering today. The West Virginia facility is expected to come online at the end of 2027.
Nscale, founded in 2024, has previously struck deals with Microsoft, according to TechCrunch.
The Nscale deal is the latest in a series of compute partnerships Anthropic has pursued over the past several months. Earlier this month, the company signed a $10 billion deal with cloud startup Volta for computing capacity from a data center in Norway. In July, Anthropic signed a $5 billion compute deal with Advanced Micro Devices. In May, the company entered a computing agreement with SpaceX that is providing $1.25 billion worth of capacity each month. Anthropic also expanded its partnerships with Amazon, Google, and Broadcom in April.
Anthropic acknowledged earlier this year that surging usage of its Claude models was taxing its systems, with the pressure showing up as degraded reliability and performance when user demand spiked.
The infrastructure push comes as Anthropic prepares for a public offering. The company submitted a confidential IPO filing to the Securities and Exchange Commission in June and has since begun making the rounds with potential investors. Anthropic investors expect the company to go public in October at a valuation of $2 trillion or more, which would make it the largest IPO in history, according to the Financial Times.
According to CNBC, how Anthropic has assembled its computing infrastructure will figure prominently in what the company tells prospective public-market investors. The company surpassed OpenAI in quarterly revenue for the first time in the second quarter, posting $11.6 billion, more than double its first-quarter total. Separately, Anthropic has been preparing to tell IPO investors that its potential revenue opportunity exceeds $30 trillion, according to The Wall Street Journal.
